title: AI Agents in Talent Acquisition
venue: Learning Day | Global Talent Acquisition (GTA) Asia, Microsoft
description:
Delivered at Microsoft Global Talent Acquisition (GTA) Asia Learning Day for an audience of close to 100, this session combined talks, a podcast-style conversation, and a live demo to show how AI agents can improve recruiting workflows end-to-end - from drafting job descriptions to extracting hiring signals and accelerating sourcing - while staying grounded in quality, consistency, and responsible human oversight.

Key Takeaways:

  • AI is most effective in talent acquisition when it augments recruiter workflows, not replaces recruiter judgment
  • High-value use cases include JD creation, skills/keyword extraction, and generating Boolean strings for sourcing
  • Reliable recruiting agents need clear instructions, scoped capabilities, relevant connectors, and guided conversation starters
  • Grounding outputs on approved templates and knowledge sources improves consistency and trust
  • Adoption improves when teams start with repeatable scenarios and iteratively refine prompts based on real usage

title: What Does Your Agent Remember About You? (And Should It?)
description:
Delivered as the youngest speaker at AI Conference 2026, this talk tackled the often-overlooked challenge of memory in AI agent systems. Using a relatable analogy — a friend who remembers every embarrassing thing you’ve ever done and brings it up at the worst moment — the session explored why agents need memory, what types exist, and the real risks when memory goes wrong.

Key Topics Covered:

  • The Amnesia Problem — why stateless sessions force users to re-explain everything, every time
  • A taxonomy of four memory types and how each works in practice
  • Real-world implementations: who’s using agent memory and what they store
  • Three failure modes: staleness (outdated facts), poisoning (injected false info), and privacy leaks
  • Ethics, regulation, and governance — should agents remember everything?
  • Open problems the field hasn’t solved yet

title: Context Engineering: The Hidden Skill Behind Production-Ready AI
description:
Presented at NextGen Data 2026 in Barcelona (virtually), this talk made the case that most production AI failures aren’t model failures — they’re context failures. Drawing an analogy to exam preparation (reading too much, going blank mid-question, or writing great answers to the wrong question), the session introduced context engineering as the critical discipline for anyone shipping AI to production.

Key Topics Covered:

  • The demo-to-production gap: why perfect demos become unreliable deployments (hallucinations, latency, spiralling costs)
  • The context window as your application’s RAM — instructions, knowledge, and tool outputs
  • Common context failure patterns and how to diagnose them
  • Practical context strategies for production systems
  • Cutting-edge patterns emerging from the field
  • Open source tools and arsenal for context engineering

title: Context Engineering: The Make-or-Break Skill for Production AI
description:
Delivered at PyConf Hyderabad 2026, this talk brought context engineering to the Python community — showing why the gap between a working demo and a reliable production AI system almost always comes down to how you fill the context window. The session used the memorable analogy of exam preparation gone wrong to drive home why ‘the model isn’t broken, the context is.’

Key Topics Covered:

  • Production reality check: perfect retrieval vs. hallucinations, snappy responses vs. unbearable latency
  • Defining the discipline: the context window as your application’s RAM (instructions, knowledge, tool outputs)
  • Common context failures and diagnostic approaches
  • Practical context strategies for Python-based AI applications
  • Cutting-edge patterns and the open source arsenal

title: Stop Hoping, Start Evaluating
venue: Future World Conversations | Future World Alliance
description:
Delivered at Future World Conversations, this talk challenged the AI community to move beyond ‘looks good enough’ and embrace systematic evaluation for AI agents. The session walked through the anatomy of an AI agent, a structured building process, and then deep-dived into why evaluations are the missing piece in most agent development workflows.

Key Topics Covered:

  • Anatomical elements of AI agents: LLMs, system prompts, tools & functions, memory & context, guardrails, and the orchestrator
  • A practical 5-step agent building process
  • Introduction to evals — what they are, why they matter, and how to design them effectively
  • Evaluation-Driven Development (EDD) as a methodology for building reliable agents
  • Tools and resources to get started with agent evaluation

title: Agent Skills: Turning Tribal Knowledge into Plug-and-play Leverage
description:
Presented to Microsoft's KITE (Design) and Copilot Extensibility teams, this session introduced Agent Skills — a new paradigm for packaging tribal knowledge into reusable, plug-and-play modules for AI coding agents. The talk made the case that prompt libraries fail because of discovery friction and personalization gaps, and showed how skills solve this by auto-loading contextual expertise only when needed.

Key Topics Covered:

  • The problem: repeated context copy-pasting, knowledge trapped in heads, and prompt libraries nobody uses
  • What Agent Skills are: folder-based packages (SKILL.md + scripts + references) — no SDK, no framework, no deployment pipeline
  • Progressive disclosure: how skills scale where system prompts don't (install 50, only 1–2 load per task)
  • Skills vs. Agents: packaged expertise for existing agents vs. autonomous loops with frameworks
  • The open standard ecosystem: write once, use in Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, and 10+ tools
  • Skill ideas built for the room: design-review, spec-writer, a11y-audit, m365-extension-spec, and more
  • Live demo: Building a skill in under 5 minutes using the skill-creator skill
  • Design principles for great skills and the sharing paradox (org-wide vs. team-level vs. personal)

title: Powering India's AI Tomorrow
venue: AI Student Summit 2026 | KLH University, Hyderabad
description:
Participated in a strategic panel discussion at the AI Student Summit 2026 (KLH University, Hyderabad), engaging with an audience of 3,500+ students on the future trajectory of Artificial Intelligence in India. The panel explored the acceleration of AI adoption across sectors, the role of India's AI startup ecosystem in driving innovation and economic advancement, and the critical dimensions of responsible and ethical AI.

Topics Discussed:

  • The future trajectory of AI in India and the acceleration of AI adoption across sectors
  • Role of the AI startup ecosystem in driving innovation and economic advancement
  • Responsible and ethical AI: policy frameworks and governance
  • Talent development and building the next generation of AI practitioners
  • Scalable AI deployment within the Indian context

title: The Authenticity Paradox: Engineering Soul into the Intelligent Age
description:
Participated in a cross-disciplinary panel debate at Manifest 2026 (organized by Framer, Creative Community & Microsoft), exploring the tension between AI-driven scale and human authenticity. The discussion challenged conventional thinking about what happens when AI products optimize for the wrong metrics, and argued for taste-driven development as a counterbalance to velocity-obsessed engineering.

Key Themes Discussed:

  • Authenticity breaks when AI scales — not because the tech fails, but because we optimize for the wrong things
  • Goodhart's Law is eating AI products: when trustworthiness becomes a score, systems test well but feel hollow
  • The trade-off future generations will regret: trading architectural integrity for velocity (10x faster builds, 10x technical debt, 1/10th the thinking)
  • The case for taste-driven development: spec-driven contracts and conscious overrides that bake judgment into systems from day one
  • The gap between vibe-coded prototypes and production — where authenticity dies

title: From Prompting to Proving: Eval-Driven AI Agent
venue: Hello Intelligence 2026 | Microsoft AI Innovators Hub, Hyderabad
description:
Delivered at Hello Intelligence 2026 (Microsoft AI Innovators Hub, Hyderabad), this talk made the case that the best AI teams don't move fast because they guess better — they move fast because they measure better. The session covered the anatomy of AI agents, a systematic building process, and deep-dived into why evaluations are the missing piece in most agent development workflows.

Key Topics Covered:

  • Anatomy of AI agents and their core building blocks
  • A 5-step process to build agents systematically
  • Why evals are not optional — turning intuition into data, and data into compounding progress
  • Evaluation-Driven Development (EDD) as a methodology
  • Tools and frameworks to get started with agent evaluation today
  • Practical advice: start small, test against reality (not happy paths), and let measurement guide you

title: Agentic Product Making
description:
Conducted a hands-on vibe-coding workshop for Microsoft's extended senior leadership team during their offsite, demonstrating how AI-powered coding with GitHub Copilot can transform engineering workflows. The session went beyond surface-level tool usage, guiding leaders through practical exercises that culminated in live demos and prototypes built in real-time.

  • Hands-on exercises: leaders building and iterating on prototypes during the session
  • Framing AI-powered development in terms of strategic value, not just capability
  • Live demo showcase: leaders sharing their prototypes and ideas built collaboratively with AI

title: Eval-Driven Agent Development
description:
Delivered at AgentJam (Global AI Community, Hyderabad), this talk shared a practitioner's perspective on Evaluation-Driven Development for AI agents. Drawing from hands-on experience building and shipping agents, the session presented a framework for making agent quality systematic rather than aspirational.

Key Topics Covered:

  • Evals velocity = product velocity: the fastest AI teams measure daily, not just build daily
  • Start small, scale systematically: begin with 10–20 representative cases, then grow the eval suite in response to real failure modes
  • Mix your methods: rule-based checks for precision & reproducibility + LLM-as-judge for nuance and ambiguity
  • Design for the real world: inject noise, embrace ambiguity, test edge cases — not just textbook inputs
  • Measurement over hope: turning "I think it works" into "here's the data — it works 87% of the time, and here's where it breaks"

title: Do Agents Do What Developers Say?
description:
Presented at the MLADS+ Agents Conference (Microsoft), this talk introduced Instruction-Following Accuracy (IF-Accuracy) — a developer-centric evaluation framework for measuring how faithfully AI agents follow the business logic encoded in their instructions. The work addressed a critical gap: existing eval rubrics judge user experience, but agentic systems need developer instruction fidelity.

Key Topics Covered:

  • The motivation: developers encode custom business logic via instructions and expect it to be followed — but only ~70% of instructions were being followed vs. 95% in benchmarks
  • Root causes of the gap: ambiguous instructions, conflicts with system prompts, tool failures, and attention bottlenecks
  • The IF-Accuracy computation pipeline: atomic instruction breakdown, turn-wise applicability assignment, conversational instruction-following analysis, and hierarchical aggregation
  • Analytics & visualization: turning raw scores into actionable insights via dashboards
  • Real customer impact: improving IF-Accuracy to 90+%, unblocking large-scale agent deployments
  • How to leverage the framework: standalone tool, internal evaluation platform integration, and extensibility to other agent platforms

  • Lab 1: Building functional AI agents with Microsoft Agent Framework

  • Security and Responsible AI (RAI) considerations
  • Verification and validation techniques for agentic systems
  • Optimization techniques for production agent deployments
  • Hands-on labs reinforcing classroom discussions throughout both days

title: Intro to Evals: The Why, What & How of Making Agent Quality a Habit
description:
Co-presented with Akhil at Microsoft's AI4All initiative (CAPE team), this workshop demystified evaluation-driven development for AI agents. Drawing from months of building, breaking, and refining agents, the session reframed evals not as unit tests but as human judgment, scaled — and walked attendees through a practical approach to making agent quality systematic.

Key Topics Covered:

  • Evals ≠ traditional QA: unit tests check "does it work?" — evals ask "does it work well, in the messy, ambiguous, human way we expect it to?"
  • Start manual: define what "good" looks like before automating with LLM-as-a-judge
  • Evals encode expertise: turning PM and domain expert intuition into repeatable signals that scale
  • Not all evals are worth automating: focus effort on high-impact, high-frequency user journeys
  • Tools amplify but don't replace thinking: using platforms to automate evals at scale, but only after defining clear scenarios, assertions, and success criteria by hand

description:
Kicked off a full-day Vibe Coding workshop for 100+ students from Heartfulness International School at Microsoft Garage, as part of the Microsoft Give Campaign. The session introduced students to AI-first development — not just typing code, but thinking with AI, co-creating with tools like GitHub Copilot, and turning curiosity into shipped projects.

  • Hands-on session: students building their own PacMan game variants from scratch
  • Publishing live games on GitHub Pages — from idea to deployed project in one session
  • Shifting mindset from "learning about tech" to creating with it

title: Gen AI Workshop
description:
A comprehensive Gen AI workshop at Aaruush ’25 (SRMIST, Chennai), delivered across two tracks. The first track covered AI agent fundamentals, agentic design patterns, and the rise of agentic protocols, with live demos building single-agent and multi-agent systems using Microsoft’s AutoGen framework. The second track focused on AI model customization and fine-tuning.

description:

The session took participants from zero to building multi-agent systems with Microsoft's AutoGen framework, proving that PMs don't need to be full-stack developers to prototype and orchestrate AI agents.

  • The AI Agent Stack: tools that matter today
  • Design patterns for AI agents

  • Production-ready systems: UI, observability, and edge cases

The highlight was watching seasoned PMs rediscover their coding spark — bridging product vision with technical possibility in real-time.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): From Buzzword to Build-Ready
description:
Co-presented with Pankaj Aher (Principal Software Engineer, Microsoft IDC) at SkillUp AI for 200+ attendees, this workshop cut through the hype around MCP (Model Context Protocol) and showed attendees how to actually build with it. The session combined architectural deep-dives with multiple live demos, covering everything from MCP primitives to creating production-ready agents that use MCP servers.

Key Topics Covered:

  • AI agents and tool use — why tools are essential for useful agents
  • Introduction to MCP: what it is, its architecture, and core primitives (with demos)
  • Ecosystem overview of available MCP servers
  • Demo: Creating an M365 Copilot Agent with MCP Tools using Agent Toolkit (ATK)
  • Demo: Creating an M365 Copilot Agent with Remote MCP Servers using Copilot Studio
  • Demo: Using MCP Servers with GitHub Copilot in VS Code
  • Security in MCP — threat models and mitigation strategies

title: Tool Use & MCP
description:
Co-presented with Kanishk Lal as part of the AI Uncovered Masterclass at STCI Microsoft, this session provided a comprehensive walkthrough of tool use in LLMs and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Starting from the evolution of function calling (ReAct, Toolformer, OpenAI API), the talk built up to MCP as the solution to the M×N integration problem, covering its architecture, primitives, and security considerations — all anchored by three live demos.

Key Topics Covered:

  • Evolution of function/tool calling: ReAct pattern, Toolformer, and OpenAI's Function Calling API
  • The M×N integration problem and how MCP transforms it into M+N
  • MCP architecture: Hosts, Clients, Servers (local & remote), and transport mechanisms (STDIO, Streamable HTTP)
  • MCP primitives: Tools, Resources, Resource Templates, Prompts, and Interactive UI Components
  • Demo 1: Creating a basic local MCP server in C# and running it in VS Code
  • Demo 2: Leveraging existing MCP servers (Playwright + MS SQL) for product research on Amazon
  • Demo 3: Transforming a fine-tuned DistilBERT sentiment classifier API into a conversational assistant via MCP
  • Security threats in MCP (Tool Poisoning, Puppet/Tool Shadowing, Rug Pull attacks) and mitigations
  • UTCP (Universal Tool Calling Protocol) as an emerging alternative and its tradeoffs vs. MCP

title: Multi-Agent Systems with LLMs for NLP
description:
Co-presented with Gurparkash Singh and Shubhojit Mallick as part of the AI Uncovered Masterclass at STCI Microsoft, this session covered the full spectrum of LLM-based AI agents and multi-agent systems. The talk progressed from foundational agent concepts and agentic design patterns through to multi-agent architectures, communication paradigms, and observability — punctuated by live demos building real multi-agent workflows with Microsoft's AutoGen framework.

Key Topics Covered:

  • LLM-based AI agents: what they are, how they differ from traditional rule-based agents, and the paradigm shift with LLMs as reasoning engines
  • Automation vs. Workflows vs. AI Agents — clarifying the distinctions
  • Memory in AI agents: debunking misconceptions (context window ≠ memory, RAG ≠ memory) and types of agent memory
  • The AI agent stack and agentic design patterns
  • Multi-Agent Systems (MAS): why they matter (complexity, scalability, robustness, specialization) and common agent roles
  • Agent communication: cooperative, competitive, and debate paradigms; centralized vs. decentralized structures; message passing vs. shared memory
  • Demo: Blog-to-Twitter Thread Scheduler using a sequential multi-agent pipeline
  • Demo: Marketing Campaign Creator using a swarm-based multi-agent architecture
  • Observability in MAS: transparency, interpretability, key metrics, and frameworks
  • Designing resilient AI agents: handling loops, timeouts, network failures, corrupted inputs, and harmful content
  • Computer-Using Agents (CUA): Claude Computer Use, OpenAI Operator, Browser-Use, Manus AI, and UI-TARS

title: Agent Building & Model Finetuning

title: Vibe Mode On! Flip the Switch to AI-First Programming
description:
Delivered to Microsoft M365 Core, this talk explored the vibe coding revolution — the shift from AI-assisted to AI-first programming. The session covered industry trends, the evolving AI coding toolkit, practical challenges like hallucinations and the context conundrum, and shared battle-tested best practices and error handling strategies for getting the most out of AI-powered development tools.

Key Topics Covered:

  • What vibe coding actually is: an AI-first, conversational style of programming that goes beyond AI-assisted coding
  • Industry trends and the growing AI coding toolkit: IDE integrations, browser-based generators, CLI tools, and Microsoft's internal tools (GitHub Copilot, Bandish, SWE Agent, Rubber Ducky)
  • Navigating major challenges: the hallucination monster and the context conundrum
  • The "AI is Dumb" fallacy — why treating your AI co-pilot like a day-one intern produces better results
  • 8 universal best practices: start with a plan, work incrementally, use Git religiously, debug with error messages, add codebase instructions, reference API docs explicitly, use annotated screenshots, and keep experimenting with models
  • Error handling strategies: Revert & Re-Prompt, Call Out Patterns, Debugging User Flows, and Visual Debugging with UI Screenshots
  • Tool-specific tips for GitHub Copilot and SWE Agent
  • What's next: agent clusters, agent fleets, and our evolving roles in an AI-first era

title: Intern Global Hackathon Kickoff
venue: The Garage (India) & The University Recruiting Team, Microsoft
description:

Alongside fellow mentors, the session tackled questions on tech stacks, time management, and how to build a hackathon prototype while juggling an internship.

Core Advice Shared:

  • Time-box your creativity: 2–3 hour focus blocks beat scattered all-nighters
  • MVP over perfection: solve the problem first, polish comes later
  • Team with opposites: the best ideas are born at intersections
  • Solve the problem, not the stack: impact matters more than the number of frameworks used
  • Reuse what exists: APIs and open-source are your friends
  • Fail fast, pivot faster: if it's not working by Day 2, switch it up
  • Build with an AI-first mindset: use GenAI to mock UIs, generate code, and brainstorm features

title: Interview with Sundar Srinivasan, VP at Microsoft Search & AI
description:

The conversation touched on work culture, mentoring, work-life balance, and advice for early-career professionals.

  • Passions beyond code: painting (three solo exhibitions), singing (YouTube covers), technical writing, and authoring the bestselling book "Beyond Code"
  • Microsoft's learning culture: sessions, workshops, conferences, and the non-technical growth in communication, personal branding, and adaptive leadership

title: Meet a Data Scientist, ML, AI & Data Science
description:

The session involved sharing personal career journeys, connecting with data enthusiasts, answering audience queries, and discussing career prospects in Data Science.

Key Takeaways Shared:

  • Focus on building a T-shaped skillset early in your career — breadth across domains, depth in one
  • It's all about the data: ML, DL, LLMs, and analytics tools are just means to efficiently solve problems
  • The art of Data Storytelling is a must-have skill — data needs to be explained and actionable insights must be derived
  • Fail fast to succeed faster — embrace experimentation and learn from setbacks
  • Leadership is a mindset, not just a job title — take initiative and show accountability
